milestone_summary: Telesensory Systems' Speech+ talking calculator for the blind, with a synthesized voice, was in use; the Kurzweil Reading Machine for the Blind (Votrax synthesizer) appeared in the same year.

quote: As I took my seat my weight set some machinery in motion. A few feet in front of me suddenly rose out of the table a large upright mirror, or such I took it to be; but instantly there appeared on its surface a grand bill of fare
claim_description: Restaurant tables with built-in screens that display a menu when the diner sits.
concept_description: A screen on which a computer shows text, graphics or data to its user, in place of printouts or dials.
milestone_summary: Whirlwind became operational in 1951, real-time output on CRT displays used in Cape Cod radar tracking

quote: You set this verse. It isn't in the copy at all.
claim_description: The linotype composes and sets original poetry on its own.
concept_description: A computer that composes stories, articles, poems or books automatically.
milestone_summary: Environment Canada deployed FoG, which generated weather forecasts in English and French from data automatically.

quote: What you hear is a combination of recorded words that are electronically put together to answer an almost infinite number of your questions.
claim_description: A computer assembles recorded speech fragments to answer a child's open-ended questions conversationally.
concept_description: A computer holding broad knowledge that answers arbitrary factual questions put to it in ordinary language.
milestone_summary: MIT's START natural-language system went online on the Internet in 1993 and answered English questions on many topics (Boris Katz, MIT)

quote: They seemed to tune themselves to the habits of their owners. They were infinitely easy to work right, and practically impossible to work wrong.
claim_description: Household appliances such as washers and TVs adapt to owners' habits, untangle laundry, and tune to the right channel automatically.
concept_description: A house whose lighting, doors, appliances and services are run automatically by machines responding to its occupants.
milestone_summary: ECHO IV served the Sutherland household's daily routines in his home through 1976.

quote: I still think people should be in love and not just mated because a calculating machine says they'll produce superior offspring.
claim_description: Computers used to select genetically optimal mates for producing superior offspring.
concept_description: A computer that pairs people as romantic partners or spouses by comparing their recorded traits.
milestone_summary: Joan Ball's St. James Computer Dating Service (later Com-Pat) in London ran its first computer match-ups of questionnaire answers on a time-shared computer.

quote: Lance, sitting flat on his back against gravity, looked up at the sweep hands on the control deck clocks and hurried through his pre-jump check list.
claim_description: Autopilot computers with preset tapes handle astrogation and the launch/jump sequence of interstellar ships.
concept_description: A computer that calculates orbits, courses and engine burns and steers a spacecraft or ship along them.
milestone_summary: Same flight: first operational use of an onboard computer for orbital maneuvers on a crewed spacecraft.

quote: Taking the disk of blue plastic from his packet, he handed it to the clerk at the desk, who dropped it into a slot in the voder in front of him. Instantly, a mechanical voice responded:
claim_description: A plastic ID disk is read by a voice-synthesizing machine that announces the holder's identity and authority.
concept_description: A machine that generates spoken language with an artificial voice, such as a talking computer reading out answers.
milestone_summary: Telesensory Systems' Speech+ talking calculator for the blind, with a synthesized voice, was in use; the Kurzweil Reading Machine for the Blind (Votrax synthesizer) appeared in the same year.
